subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A cam and follower mechanism is used to convert:
questions.explain: As a cam rotates, its profile pushes the follower up and down, converting rotary motion into reciprocating motion.

questions.q: In a pulley system, adding more pulleys (more supporting ropes) generally:
options: Reduces the effort needed to lift the load
Increases the effort needed to lift the load
questions.explain: More supporting rope sections share the load, so less effort is needed to lift it, though the rope must be pulled further.

questions.q: For a simple gear train, the gear ratio is calculated as:
options: Driven teeth added to driver teeth
Driven teeth divided by driver teeth
Driver teeth divided by driven teeth
Driver teeth multiplied by driven teeth
questions.explain: Gear ratio equals the number of teeth on the driven gear divided by the number on the driver gear.

questions.q: Mechanical advantage is gained when a mechanism allows:
options: A larger effort to move a smaller load
A small effort to move a larger load
No load to be moved at all
Energy to be created from nothing
questions.explain: Mechanical advantage means a machine lets a small input effort overcome a larger output load.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.explain: Wind is a renewable source that naturally replenishes, unlike the finite fossil fuels coal, gas and oil.

questions.q: A driver gear has 10 teeth and the driven gear has 30 teeth. The gear ratio is:
questions.explain: Gear ratio = driven 30 divided by driver 10 = 3, written 3:1, meaning the driver turns three times for each turn of the driven gear.

questions.q: Motion that moves back and forth in a straight line is called:
questions.explain: Reciprocating motion is repeated back-and-forth movement in a straight line, as seen in a piston or a sewing-machine needle.

questions.q: A rechargeable battery stores energy in which form?
questions.explain: A battery stores energy chemically and converts it to electrical energy when it discharges through a circuit.

questions.q: In a gear train, an idler gear is added mainly to:
options: Change the overall gear ratio of the train
Reverse the direction of the output gear without changing the ratio
questions.explain: An idler gear sits between driver and driven gears to reverse the output's direction; it does not affect the overall gear ratio.

questions.q: Motion that swings back and forth on a pivot, like a pendulum, is called:
questions.explain: Oscillating motion swings back and forth around a fixed pivot point, as a pendulum does.

questions.q: A first-class lever, such as a seesaw, has the fulcrum positioned:
options: At the same point as the load
Only at the very end of the load
Between the effort and the load
Beyond both the effort and load
questions.explain: In a first-class lever the fulcrum (pivot) sits between the effort and the load, as on a seesaw or pair of scissors.

questions.q: A force that pulls or stretches a material is called:
questions.explain: Tension is a pulling or stretching force, while compression is a squashing force.
